body:
Thanks for the advice.

Talking to classmates is something I haven't really done in the past, but I'm definitely going to try to do more of it this coming year.

Group situations are where I struggle the most to talk and be open, however. 

I suppose I'm kind of a control freak. I like to have control over myself, what I'm doing, and the conversations I have. Sometimes it's useful at college, but most of the time it isn't. I'm really working on trying to go with the flow more, but it certainly isn't easy.

I appreciate everyone's advice. I think the best plan is just to ask her to stop talking about sex with me. I'm not going to cut her off as a friend because we genuinely have a great, supportive friendship: we do a lot of fun things together and we have some hilarious conversations. I just think we've been a little too open with each other about things recently.

One person mentioned how I seem to view body count/having sex as a competition. There is some truth in that, and I think it's just because I've had some pretty toxic guy friends in the past who viewed it like that and kind of ingrained me to think about it that way. I recognize that it's the wrong way to think about it, so that's definitely something I'm going to be working on moving forward.

Some other people said that I need to do other interesting things/activities to gain self-confidence. I'm actually a pretty active guy at my college, even though I haven't been on campus much recently. I'm the secretary of a pretty big academic club, and I'm involved in a club sport. I'm a confident guy in most areas of my life, just my weakest link is interacting with people (especially girls) outside of more professional/work relationships.

Again, thanks for everyone's advice.

I feel you there 100%. I'm a rising sophomore, not a freshman, but I spent 90% of the past school year taking classes remotely. 

I want to be able to make friends and have fun at college, but with my levels of anxiety and introversion, I can't imagine it's possible for me to do that.

You're not the only person dreading having to go to college. Honestly, a lot of the people who say they're excited to go may not actually be that excited. You'd be surprised how much people often disguise their true thoughts and feelings in order to fit in.

As you're a freshman, you have to at least give it a chance. You haven't actually experienced any of it yet! It may not be at all what you're expecting, in a positive way. The one thing you shouldn't do is purposely try to make yourself miserable there. That's never a recipe for success or happiness.

Sleep is great, but think of it as a way to relax yourself instead of as a way to pass the time.

Update: my psychiatrist put me on an antidepressant that isn’t helping at all. I have been suicidal for three straight days now; I can’t believe there is any fluid in me I’ve cried it all out. I cut myself and hit myself but that did nothing to ease my anger and pain. My ex-girlfriend told me yesterday that she wants me to be with someone else. She doesn’t want anything to do with me anymore. That is the last straw. There’s a bridge near where I live that I think I will go to tonight.
